To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
recovery of a temperate reef assemblage following the cessation of tow fishing has been demonstrated.
a temperate reef assemblage has recovered in the Lyme Bay MPA following the cessation of tow demersal fishing.
recovery of a temperate reef assemblage following the cessation of tow demersal fishing was observed within 3 years.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the recovery of a temperate rocky reef community following a cessation of fishing disturbance and the subsequent implications to the wider ecosystem and commercial fisheries.
the recovery of temperate reef assemblages in Lyme Bay following the exclusion of towed demeral fishing gear.

the following: • Quantifying the response of benthic communities to the cessation of tow demersal fishing in the Lyme Bay MPA • Identifying the key processes that drive the recovery of benthic community composition • Identifying the potential for ecosystem recovery in terms of the provision of goods and services • Assessing the timescale of recovery of benthos following the cessation of tow-demersal fishing • Assessing the impact of the cessation of tow fishing on the provision of goods & services
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the New Closure is becoming more like the Closed Controls and unlike the Open Controls, and is therefore recovering from the effects of towed demesal fishing.

‘within three years of the cessation of tow demersal fishing in Lyme Bay MPA the New Closure has become more similar to the previously voluntarily closed areas, and less similar to those areas that have remained open to fishing’.
the New Closure is recovering towards the Closed Control and is becoming increasingly different from the Open Controls.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are observing recovery, and this is likely to continue.
the Lyme Bay MPA is a successful example of the potential of MPAs to deliver ecosystem benefits and that the recovery of the benthic community in the New Closure has been rapid.
recovery of the Lyme Bay MPA benthos is evident and is progressing rapidly.
The main takeaway from our work is that
recovery of benthic communities is possible within three years of cessation of towed-demersal fishing.
recovery of temperate reefs can occur within 3 years of the cessation of demersal fishing disturbance.
MPAs can be effective in the recovery of marine benthic communities and the ecosystem services they provide.
